_meta: A stored image grid and its EXIF orientation tag, used to show that pixel data is stored in the camera sensor's native orientation with a separate tag saying how to rotate it for display, so a pipeline that reads the raw pixels and ignores the tag shows the image sideways -- and, worse, a pipeline that strips the EXIF tag without first applying it loses the orientation permanently. Cameras write pixels in a fixed sensor order and record how the camera was held as an Orientation tag (1 = already upright, 3 = 180 degrees, 6 = rotate 90 clockwise for display, 8 = rotate 90 counter-clockwise, plus mirrored variants). A correct viewer applies the tag before showing the image; a naive tool that decodes the raw pixel array and treats it as the final image displays a portrait photo lying on its side. The real trap is re-encoding: many pipelines strip metadata when they resize or convert, and if they drop the orientation tag without first baking the rotation into the pixels, the image is now stored sideways with a tag of 1 (upright) -- the information that would have corrected it is gone, and every future viewer shows it wrong. The fix is to APPLY the orientation to the pixels (physically rotate the array) and only then set the tag to 1, so the stored pixels are upright and no tag is needed. On this fixture the stored grid is 2 rows by 3 columns with tag 6, so the correct display is the grid rotated 90 clockwise to 3 rows by 2 columns; ignoring the tag shows the raw 2x3 grid (wrong), stripping the tag leaves the raw 2x3 grid with tag 1 (wrong and unrecoverable), and baking rotates to 3x2 and sets tag 1 (correct). The stored grid and its tag are the fixture; the correct display, and the result of ignoring, stripping, and baking, are computed. Stdlib only.
